title: Mobilising the Masses for the Invasion
author: Che Guevara
context: Delivered to sugar workers in Santa Clara on March 28, 1961, merely twenty days before the CIA-sponsored Bay of Pigs invasion (Playa Girón), this speech prepares the Cuban working class for imminent imperialist military aggression and outlines the necessity of unyielding national resistance.
relatesToToday: Provides crucial lessons on anti-imperialist vigilance, national self-reliance, and mass mobilization against external military aggression and economic destabilization.
keyTakeaways: The Cuban Revolution demonstrated that colonized peoples can rise up and defeat imperialism directly under its fangs.
Imperialist aggression must be met with continuous, decisive counter-blows without taking a single step backward.
A revolution cannot depend solely on external foreign aid: true security stems from the unity and sacrifice of the organized working class.
